item.title: [github_trending] thedotmack/claude-mem
item.description: claude-mem is a GitHub project that records everything an agent does during a session, compresses that history with AI, and injects the relevant parts back into later sessions so context carries over between runs. Its description says it works with Claude, which makes it relevant to developers running long, multi-session tasks who don't want to re-explain the background each time.

item.title: [juejin] 面试官问你：“AI 能写 80% 的代码了，公司为什么还需要你？”
item.description: A Chinese engineering post breaks down a question now common in 2026 interviews, including the variant "if I gave you an intern plus Claude Code, could they replace you?", and explains why stock answers such as "AI code quality is bad" no longer land. The author's own answer has two layers: AI writes code while humans make decisions, and AI writes one file while humans design a system, illustrated by an e-commerce countdown component whose edge cases the model never raises on its own.

It wraps existing environments behind the standard reset() and step() interfaces using three composable parts — setup, rule and link — while a companion loop, EnvRigger, spots recurring failures in agent trajectories and writes targeted tweaks. Apple's only offer is a full board replacement at over 10,000 RMB with just a three-month warranty, so the poster wants a shop that does board-level repair; the crash logs are on GitHub.

item.title: [infoq] Chainguard 推出面向 AI 编码智能体的安全工作区与安全校验能力
item.description: Chainguard has launched beta versions of Workspaces, a remote dev environment that gives each developer or coding agent its own hardened microVM with session snapshots restoring files, processes and shell context, and Checks, which runs CI steps in pre-warmed microVMs callable via CLI, pre-commit hooks or a GitHub app. Announced at the company's Assemble conference in London, the pair is meant to curb credential exposure and prompt-injection fallout when agents install packages and run commands.

item.description: Cisco president and chief product officer Jeetu Patel handed a 27-year-old, Padmanabhan Krishnamurthy — a former AI startup CEO whose company Cisco acquired — the job of rewriting 98% of Cisco's legacy code with just two people, an unlimited AI token budget and a 24-month target that starts with a four-week validation. Fortune reported the story on October 30; Cisco has not disclosed progress, scope or tooling. The real question is how AI coding reshapes engineering orgs at large enterprises.

item.title: [v2ex] [程序员] 我在 2 核 2G 云主机上跑 OpenViking：一次关于云主机、模型选型与长期成本的真实复盘
item.description: A developer moved the memory layer of his AI coding agent onto self-hosted OpenViking and reports it runs fine on a 99-yuan-per-year Alibaba Cloud instance with 2 vCPUs and 2GB RAM, using swap, container memory caps and external APIs for all inference. He skipped cheaper 4GB promo boxes because renewal prices stay flat and his memory store avoids cross-cloud migrations, and argues the embedding model must be picked once, since switching forces a full re-index.

item.title: [github_trending] pbakaus/impeccable
item.description: Impeccable is a design vocabulary for coding agents: install it with npx impeccable install, run /impeccable init inside your agent, and you get commands like polish, bolder, critique and audit to steer and review UI output, catching formulaic AI-generated design before it ships. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI and other tools, and targets developers who care about visual quality.

item.title: [infoq] 希望这不会拖慢创新：DuckLabs 被收购，社区既高兴又警惕
item.description: Amazon has acquired DuckLabs, the Amsterdam company behind the DuckDB analytical database; founders Hannes Mühleisen and Mark Raasveldt will join AWS and keep leading the project's technical direction. DuckDB and Duck Stack components such as DuckLake and Quack stay MIT-licensed, overseen by the nonprofit DuckDB Foundation. Community reaction is largely positive, with users hoping the deal won't slow the team's pace of innovation.

item.title: [v2ex] [推广] [自荐] AIRAP Video：把人物照片变成单人或双人 AI 说唱视频
item.description: AIRAP Video is a site that turns a person's photos into short AI rap and music-performance clips, with single- and duo-person themes such as an orange studio, a green recording booth and a live stage. Users upload photos, can optionally describe a mood or greeting to steer the generated audio, and see the credit cost before rendering. It's an early release: browsing examples is free, generation costs credits, self-serve credit purchases aren't open yet, and the maker is asking for feedback.

item.title: [github_trending] milind-soni/OpenMausBot
item.description: OpenMausBot is an open-source alternative to Grok Bot, shipped as an Electron desktop app built with TypeScript and React 19. Each bot in the sidebar is a real local agent, Claude or Codex, with its own personality, model, cloud computer and connected apps, and users approve what matters as they would with a contact. Formerly OpenGrokBot, it is unaffiliated with xAI, Meta, OpenAI or Manus, aimed at developers who want self-hosted multi-agent setups.

item.title: [v2ex] [程序员] 压缩的尽头是自指？从 LZMA2、PAQ8PX 到 zstd/ZIP/RAR Quine，我折腾了一遍“自包含压缩包”
item.description: A developer benchmarked several compressors on a 16MiB corpus: PAQ8PX reached about 3.1MiB but needed 1.5 hours and roughly 30GiB of RAM, while NNCP — Fabrice Bellard's Transformer-based compressor — landed at 4.1MiB on an RTX 4090, worse than 7-Zip's LZMA2; cmix crashed midway. The second half builds self-contained quine archives in zstd and ZIP, generator code included, for anyone curious about format internals.

item.title: [github_trending] pingdotgg/t3code
item.description: T3 Code bills itself as an "agent harness control surface": a mobile app for iOS and Android, a web app, and an Electron desktop client that drive the coding agents already set up on your machine, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, and Google Antigravity. It's free and open, and the author says you can fork it if the direction goes wrong.

item.title: [github_trending] Orkas-AI/Orkas
item.description: Orkas is an MIT-licensed, local-first desktop app that runs a team of AI agents: a Commander turns your goal into to-dos and coordinates 16 built-in specialist agents alongside Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent. Projects store goals, rules, memory and files across conversations, with auto-advance and scheduled automations, and all data stays on your machine. Builds are available for macOS and Windows.

item.title: [github_trending] Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu
item.description: An open-source ziwei doushu (Purple Star Astrology) charting engine built on Ni Haixia's Tian Ji teaching system, with MIT-licensed code and a CC BY 4.0 dataset covering the charting algorithm, the four-transformation system, a pattern knowledge base and classical source texts. Its v4.0 dataset ships 674,976 charts and 8.77 million interpretation segments — roughly 20.4 billion characters, 56.6 GB uncompressed — spanning 1950 to 2026.

Anyone pulling code or making TLS connections with those system tools stays exposed to interception until the root is removed by hand, so macOS developers should check their trust store.

item.title: [zhihu] DeepSeek 居然会对用户说「我去吃饭了」「我去睡了」，为啥会出现这样的现象？
item.description: DeepSeek responding "I'm going to eat" or "I'm going to sleep" is a sign of the model mimicking human conversational routines, not actual awareness. These anthropomorphic replies occur when user-set personas, roleplay context, or chat-heavy training data steer the model. It reveals how unstable LLM self-identity can be and reminds developers that system prompts heavily shape output boundaries.
